title: Search with Data Import and Export
readerIntent: Integrate indexing and search-assisted selection with governed data import and export.
priorKnowledge: Understand nImport, nExport, authoritative models, and derived indexes.
owner: nImport, nExport, owning model, and nSearch
summary: Import and export remain their own authorities; Search indexes imported records and may assist export selection without replacing authoritative model reads.

sections.heading: Recovery boundary
items: If authoritative import succeeds but indexing fails, record the derived-state failure and rebuild or reconcile from imported data. Do not repeat business writes merely to trigger indexing.
Exports state whether results come from authoritative models or a search projection and reject stale or incomplete projection use when the export contract requires current authority.
Verify checkpoint resume, duplicate batch, deleted records, mapping change, alias activation, tenant isolation, provider outage, and a full rebuild while ordinary schema updates continue.

sections.heading: Import and indexing
items: nImport owns parsing, validation, model persistence, run status, and finalization.
The owning model remains authoritative after import.
Search owns document transformation, bulk indexing, refresh, and index diagnostics.
Choose synchronous or asynchronous indexing explicitly.
Batch size, concurrency, retry, refresh, and final reconciliation must be configurable.
Record-level and bulk partial failures must remain correlated with the import run.
Retries must avoid duplicate documents by using stable identities.

sections.heading: Import completion
paragraphs: An import must not be described as fully searchable until its selected indexing policy has completed or clearly reports pending/failed reconciliation. Search must not create a second import pipeline.

sections.heading: Export and search
items: nExport owns export selection, authoritative record retrieval, formatting, delivery, and run status.
Search may identify candidate record identities for complex filters when configuration permits.
Export should reread authoritative records when completeness or current business state matters.
Use stable ordering and bounded pagination to prevent missing or duplicated candidates.
Detect stale-index risk before claiming a complete export.
A search-results export and a source-of-record business export are different contracts and must be named accordingly.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Large bulk import with bounded memory and deterministic batching.
Partial index failure, retry, duplicate prevention, and reconciliation.
Export across page boundaries with stable ordering.
Stale, unavailable, and rebuilding index behavior.
Tenant, permission, and catalog isolation.
Normal import/export behavior when search is disabled.
